request.prompt: These are 9 consecutive axial slices (superior to inferior, 1.25 mm spacing) from a low-dose chest CT, cropped to a 64 mm field of view centred on one structure in the lung. Is the structure at the centre of the images a cross-section of a blood vessel or a pulmonary nodule? Answer with one word, Vessel or Nodule, then one short sentence of reasoning, then the estimated diameter in mm.

content.thinking:
This round structure persists over about 11mm across all slices, sitting near vessels — that persistence makes me think of a nodule near the hilum, though I need to rule out a vessel running craniocaudally since those also look round in cross-section. The bilobed appearance suggests it could be a nodule attached to or abutting a vessel rather than the vessel itself.

Given the constant size and shape across all 9 slices spanning about 10mm, this is most consistent with a vessel seen in cross-section running vertically through the plane, roughly 7mm in diameter.

content.text: **Vessel.** The bright, rounded structure keeps the same size and position across all 9 slices (>10 mm craniocaudally) and connects to branching tubular opacities, consistent with a perihilar pulmonary vessel running perpendicular to the axial plane rather than a spherical nodule. Estimated diameter: ~7 mm.
